text:
alex: quick async standup — kernel / batching / KV / perf bench. TL;DR: pushed a prefetch tweak to canary, saw ~6% p99 latency win but ~+2% cost on our adaptive batch scenario. Blocker: eviction regressions on smaller GPUs causing warmup OOMs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821

maya: nice. what's the canary config? batch target? model? :eyes:

alex: canary = kernel-prefetch-v2, batch target = adaptive up to 32, running on g4dn-xlarge. model used for the run = rw-13b-qlora. quick bench details: single-tenant qps ~1200, avg tokens 30. logs show `p99 before=124ms after=117ms` (consistent across three runs).

ryan: fyi i reproced spikes tied to KV eviction when concurrent requests > 20. stack traces point to `kv::evict()` thrashing. adding `--kv-evict-delay=25ms` stabilizes in my repro. may need hot-key isolation or per-shard soft caps.

alex: thanks — blocker: on A10g we saw OOMs during warmup because prefetch fills prefix cache aggressively. need a transient cap on prefix caching per-model/shard; opening issue now.

jen: i can take the eviction policy change. plan: implement soft_limit per-shard for prefix cache, then fallback to streaming prefix reads when over threshold. i'll open a draft PR today.

liam: perf bench note: I ran microbatching with `group-merge` toggled. enabled `group-merge` = +8% throughput, tail latency stable. will upload flamegraph and throughput CSV to http://bench.internal/redwood/21834 later today.

alex: code-review ping @maya @ryan on #4821 — need approvals to roll canary to 10%. also want to ensure tests cover eviction edgecases.

maya: i'll review by EOD. quick q: did you measure cost / 1k tokens? earlier runs showed +2% cost overall.

alex: yep. cost/1k went up slightly due to extra warmup traffic: `cost_before=0.88c cost_after=0.898c` — ~1.9% delta. expectation is net win after cache warms and tail improves.

dev-bot: deploy started for kernel-prefetch-v2 at 2183456900 on 2 hosts. Monitor: https://console.redwood/deploys/2183456900 :rocket:

ryan: quick ask — can we emit `kv.prefetch.hit_ratio` per-model? current metric is aggregated globally and it's hard to attribute.

jen: agreed, i'll add a per-model `kv.prefetch.hit_ratio` gauge in the runtime PR. should we tag it for Q2 telemetry work?

liam: infra note — no blockers from infra. i'll schedule an overnight infra run with eviction tuning and small-GPU warmup to validate.

maya: reviewed and left small comments. LGTM pending test fixes. flagged a flaky `batcher_test` that seems timing sensitive.

alex: great. i'll respond to comments and hold the rollout at 10% until tests are green. thanks all :heart:
